title: Laolaizi Plays the Child
text:
Laolaizi was a recluse of the state of Chu who, according to tradition, cared for his parents with great devotion. Even when he himself was seventy years old, his parents were still alive, and he worried that seeing their son grown old would remind them of their own age and sadden them.

So he never spoke of being old. He dressed in brightly colored clothes like a little child and played on the floor in front of them, making childish noises to amuse them.

Once, carrying water into the hall for his parents, he slipped and fell. Rather than let them worry that he had hurt himself, or be reminded of his age, he lay on the ground and wailed like a baby, and his parents laughed at the sight.

The story became one of the Twenty Four Filial Exemplars, the collection of tales of devotion to parents that was read and illustrated across China, Korea and Japan for centuries. Pictures of the white-haired man in bright child's clothing, tumbling in front of his parents, were among the most familiar images in the series.
lesson: Caring for elderly parents is not only about meeting needs. It also means protecting their spirits, and sometimes setting aside your own dignity to make them laugh.
source: Guo Jujing, The Twenty Four Filial Exemplars (Ershisi Xiao), Yuan dynasty; earlier in Liu Xiang's Lienu zhuan
caveat: Laolaizi is a semi-legendary figure and the episode is a traditional tale.
